title: Heat Pump Rebates in Fort St. John 2026: Up to $4,000
desc: Fort St. John heat pump rebates for 2026: up to $4,000 for replacing electric heat, plus up to $1,000 until Oct 31. January lows of -15.0°C, local homes and top-rated installers.
h1: Heat Pump Rebates in Fort St. John
badge: Up to $4,000, plus up to $1,000 until Oct 31
lead: Fort St. John has the coldest winters of any city we cover in BC. A heat pump can still earn rebates here, but sizing and backup heat matter more than anywhere else.
cards_heading: What heat pump rebates pay in Fort St. John
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's heat pump rebate page on October 3, 2026. These rebates are for homes that heat with electricity today. The CleanBC amounts are for income-qualified households only.

cards.title: BC Hydro whole home
cards.note: Replacing electric heat; the heat pump meets 100% of the load at -5°C.

cards.title: BC Hydro partial
cards.note: The heat pump meets at least half of the heating load.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Installed, invoiced and paid August 1 to October 31, 2026. Apply by November 30, 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified (CleanBC)
cards.note: Level 1 switching from gas, oil or propane to a central or 3+ head system. Level 2 up to $7,000, Level 3 up to $3,500. From electric heat, Level 1 only, up to $5,000.

cards.title: Northern top-up
cards.note: Income Level 1 and 2 households at or north of 100 Mile House on BC Hydro.

after_cards:
A Fort St. John example

An income Level 1 household in a gas-heated Fort St. John house installs a central heat pump through a CleanBC registered contractor. The Energy Savings Program pays up to $13,000, and the northern top-up adds up to $3,000.
sections: Fort St. John's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -15.0°C, and the coldest reading was -42.2°C. BC Hydro tests the whole-home rebate at -5°C, which is ten degrees warmer than a normal January night here. NRCan field tests measured a cold-climate heat pump's efficiency (COP) dropping to about 1.5 at -21.1°C. Below that, many units shut off. Plan on backup heat that can carry the whole house on the coldest nights.
The 2021 Census counted 8,775 households in Fort St. John. About 58% own and 50% live in a detached house (4,375 homes). Of all households, 2,035 own a detached house built before 1981.
The northern top-up for income-qualified homes

Fort St. John is north of 100 Mile House and on BC Hydro, so income-qualified households switching from gas, oil or propane can get the CleanBC northern top-up of up to $3,000 on top of the Energy Savings Program amount (Levels 1 and 2). This is the only way to reach $16,000 ($13,000 plus $3,000), and it is only for Level 1 households.
Only for homes replacing electric heat

BC Hydro's heat pump rebate is only for homes that are heated mainly by electricity today: baseboards or an electric furnace. If your home heats with natural gas, oil or propane, BC Hydro pays nothing for the switch. The gas-to-heat-pump rebate for all households ended on April 11, 2025. Income-qualified households can still use the CleanBC Energy Savings Program.
What the heat pump must do

For the $4,000 whole-home rebate, the heat pump must keep 22°C inside at -5°C outside, shown by a CSA F280-12 heat loss calculation. It must be on BC Hydro's eligible list, with HSPF2 of 8.5 or higher and SEER2 of 15.2 or higher. A home over 1,200 square feet needs a multi-split or central system. If the unit meets at least half your heat, it can earn the $1,500 partial rebate instead.

BC Hydro is adding up to $1,000 for heat pumps that are installed, invoiced and paid between August 1 and October 31, 2026. Apply by November 30, 2026. It is first come, first served. After October 31, the normal $4,000 and $1,500 amounts still apply.
installers_intro: These Fort St. John heat pump installers have the best Google ratings with enough reviews to trust. Ratings and review counts from Google Maps. Ask each one if they are HPCN members.
claim_steps: Check your bill: BC Hydro or FortisBC, and confirm your home heats with electricity.
Hire a contractor in the Home Performance Contractor Network (required since June 1, 2026).
Get a CSA F280-12 heat loss calculation and the model's AHRI number in the quote.
Install, then pay the invoice in full.
Apply online within six months of the invoice date.
faq: Will a heat pump work at -40°C in Fort St. John?
Most will not run at that temperature. They work well in milder weather and hand over to backup heat on the coldest nights. Ask the installer at what temperature it stops.
Is the northern top-up for everyone?
No. It is for income Level 1 and 2 households in the CleanBC Energy Savings Program, at or north of 100 Mile House, on BC Hydro.
Do I need an HPCN contractor?
Yes. Since June 1, 2026, BC Hydro pays only for installs by a Home Performance Contractor Network member. Self-installs do not qualify.
Can I get a rebate if I heat with gas?

Not from the utility rebate. It is only for replacing electric heat. Income-qualified households can use the CleanBC Energy Savings Program, which pays up to $13,000 at Level 1 for central or 3+ head systems.
How long do I have to apply?
Six months from the invoice date for BC Hydro. For the limited-time bonus, apply by November 30, 2026.
